== Device tag matching in automation sessions

A device tag name now matches only tags that are visible to you: _Org_ tags and your own _Me_ tags. Another user's _Me_ tag never matches your session request, even when it has the same name as an _Org_ tag.

* Fixed an issue where a session request that selected devices by several device tags found no device and timed out when one of the tag names was also used by another user's _Me_ tag in the same organization.
* When `kobiton:deviceTagType` or the Turbo Test Execution `device_tag_type` parameter is set to `private`, only your own _Me_ tags match.
* In the Kobiton API v2, the tag name filter of `GET /v2/devices` ignores other users' _Me_ tags, and `tags.private_tags` lists only your own _Me_ tags.

A request that matched devices only through another user's _Me_ tag no longer matches those devices.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:capabilities/available-capabilities.adoc#_kobitondevicetags[kobiton:deviceTags].

// Source: KOB-55843 from PR #1019

== Provisioning profile details for iOS app versions

The version details of an iOS app in *Apps* now include a *Signing* section that shows what the app's provisioning profile covers.

* The *Signing* section shows the profile type, devices covered, profile expiration date, and entitlements.
* For Ad Hoc and Development profiles, *Devices covered* shows how many of your lab's iOS devices are included in the profile.
* Versions uploaded before signing analysis was available show `Not analyzed yet`.
* In the Kobiton API, the `signing` object in v2 app and app version responses includes `devices_covered`, with `covered` and `total` device counts.

For details, see xref:apps:app-metadata.adoc#_signing[Signing].

== iOS sessions use the app build that matches the device

Automation sessions that install an app with `kobiton-store:<appId>` now select the newest version built for the device type. An iOS Simulator gets the newest Simulator build, and a real iOS device gets the newest real-device build. Previously, the newest version was used regardless of build type, which caused generic system errors or apps that never opened.

* When an app has no build for the device type, or the requested version is built for a different device type, no session is created and nothing is installed. A message explains the build type mismatch instead of a generic install error.
* Installing a build of the wrong type through the Kobiton CLI, the Kobiton API, or an app install command during an automation session now fails with the same message. Previously, some of these installs reported success even though the app could not run.
* The behavior is consistent across Appium sessions and native XCUITest sessions.

Android apps, and iOS apps whose build type matches the device, are unaffected.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:capabilities/available-capabilities.adoc#_app_ios_build_types[iOS build types].

=== Analytics reports

* Fixed an issue where long table values in PNG exports of analytics reports, such as iOS UDIDs in the *Most Used Devices* table of the Usage Dashboard, overlapped the next column.
** Each table column is now sized to fit its values, and the image widens to fit the widest table.
** A value that is too long for its column ends with an ellipsis (…) instead of overlapping the next column.
** PNG exports are drawn at twice the previous resolution, so text stays sharp when zoomed.
** CSV exports are unchanged.

// Source: KOB-55538 from PR #1016
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/1016

== Scriptless automation improvements

* Fixed an issue where a screen rotation captured in a baseline session was not replayed during a Scriptless test run. The device stayed in its original orientation, so later steps could not find their elements.
** A rotation to landscape now rotates the device during the test run on Android and iOS. A rotation back to portrait is also replayed.
** Existing test cases that include a rotation now replay it correctly, without re-recording.
** Taps and swipes captured after a rotation land on the intended position.
** If the app under test cannot rotate, the test run continues instead of stopping.

// Source: KOB-55659 from PR #1015
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/1015

== Report descriptions and Category filter in Analytics Reports

The Analytics Reports page shows what each report is for and lets you filter the list by category.

* A *Description* column replaces the *Last synced at* column in the reports list. Long descriptions are shortened. Hover over a shortened description to see the full text.
* Each report page shows the report description below *Last synced*.
* A *Category* filter next to *Search* narrows the list to the selected categories. Search text and selected categories apply together.

// Source: KOB-56746 from PR #1014
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/1014

* *API response types:* Some API fields read from 64-bit database columns are now returned as JSON numbers instead of numeric strings. Integrations that parse these fields as strings should also accept numbers:
** `GET /v2/test-cases/{testCaseId}`: `steps[].order_id`.
** `GET /v2/validations` and `GET /v2/validations/flex-correct`: `items[].command_id` and `items[].test_step.order_id`.
** `GET /v2/test-runs/{testRunId}` with revisit actions included: `order_id` on each revisit action, live remediation action and agent action.
** The usage report endpoints under `/v1/predefined-report/usage-report/` (Appium script, crash, response time and accessibility validation): the `nQuantities` and `nScreens` counts.
** The MCP tools that return the same data (`getTestCase`, `listFlexCorrects`).
+
Command IDs in other API responses were already numbers and are unchanged.
* *Test run details:* For a test run with 10 or more devices or test cases, `GET /v2/test-runs/{testRunId}` now lists them in their run order (1, 2, … 10) instead of text order (1, 10, 2, …).

== More reliable Lightning Mode connections

Lightning Mode sessions on iOS and Android devices start and stay connected more reliably.

* Lightning Mode no longer ends while it is starting, or about a second after it starts, when the browser repeats the final step of setting up the secure connection.
* If the secure connection for the device stream can't be set up, the session now ends with an error instead of staying open with no video.
* In browsers that support AES-GCM encryption, such as Chrome, the Lightning Mode stream now uses AES-GCM. Other browsers continue to use the same encryption as before.

=== Lightning mode security update

Gigacap now includes libnice 0.1.24, the networking library that Lightning mode uses to connect to devices. This version fixes a heap overflow vulnerability in TURN relay connections over TCP.

Lightning mode sessions on iOS and Android devices work the same as before.

== Accurate error message when a device is still being released

Fixed an issue where starting an Appium session on a device that was still being released from the previous session returned `There are no devices that satisfy your filter criteria`, even though the device matched the requested capabilities.

* While a matching device is still being released, the session request returns a message that the device is in a cleanup session. Retry the request after the device is released.
* Appium Turbo Test sessions return a message that the device is in use when the matching device is in use by another session.

=== deviceConnect

* Fixed an issue where macOS Local Network privacy blocked deviceConnect on macOS 15 and later after a deviceConnect update. Blocked connections to the Kobiton Portal or to Bluetooth modules on the host machine's subnet were reported only as `No route to host` or `Network unreachable`.
* Added a message that names macOS Local Network privacy as the cause when it blocks deviceConnect, and points to *System Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network*. The message appears as a banner in the deviceConnect Console and on its login page, and in the error for an affected Bluetooth module.

After installing this update, macOS hosts that reach a Kobiton Portal or Bluetooth module on their own subnet ask once to allow `dc-services` to find devices on local networks. Choose *Allow*. Later deviceConnect updates keep this approval. Connections to Kobiton Cloud and other routed connections are not affected.

== Per-app re-sign mode for iOS apps in the Kobiton API

The Kobiton API now stores a re-sign mode for each iOS app and returns the mode that applies to the app. The mode applies to every version of the app, including versions uploaded later.

* Set an iOS app's re-sign mode with the new `PUT /v2/apps/{id}/resign-mode` endpoint. Accepted values are `ORG_DEFAULT`, `AUTO`, `ALWAYS`, and `NEVER`.
* Every existing and newly uploaded iOS app starts with `ORG_DEFAULT`. While an app uses `ORG_DEFAULT`, its effective mode is the organization's default re-sign mode.
* `GET /v2/apps` and `GET /v2/apps/{id}` return three new fields for iOS apps: `resign_mode`, `effective_mode`, and `inherited`. `GET /v1/apps` and `GET /v1/apps/{id}` return the same fields as `resignMode`, `effectiveMode`, and `inherited`. Apps on other platforms don't include these fields.
* The app's uploader, an organization admin, or a user whose role has the *View all applications* permission can change the mode.
* The endpoint returns `400` for an app that isn't an iOS app or for a value other than the four accepted values. It returns `404` if you can't see the app or aren't allowed to change it.

If your API client validates responses against a strict schema, update the schema to allow the new fields on iOS apps.

== Appium 2 sessions start after a deviceConnect upgrade on macOS hosts

* Fixed an issue where, after deviceConnect was upgraded on a macOS host, Appium 2 sessions that set `kobiton:runtime` to `appium` could fail to start on that host with a DC-500 error. Xium sessions and other sessions that don't set `kobiton:runtime` to `appium` were not affected.
* Installing a deviceConnect build that includes this fix repairs an affected macOS host without a restart.

== Network payload capture setup no longer fails intermittently on iOS devices that use Option 2

On iOS devices set up for network payload capture with Option 2 (manually import and trust the certificate), capture setup now completes when a session is launched from Kobiton Portal while an app is open on the device. Previously, setup could fail and the session ran without capturing network traffic.

* Sessions on iOS and Android devices now start on the app that was open on the device, instead of on the home screen.
* Network payload capture on Android devices is unchanged.

See xref:devices:local-devices/network-payload-capture/index.adoc[].

== Security updates for Standalone

- The Kobiton Portal, user guide, and help widget images for Standalone deployments now use nginx 1.30.7. This update addresses known security vulnerabilities in the web server and system packages of the previous images.
- The user guide and help widget move from the nginx 1.31.x mainline release to the 1.30.7 stable release, so security scanners may report a lower nginx version number for these images than before.
- Web server configuration and served content are unchanged.

== Apps install on iOS Simulators at the start of Appium sessions

When an Appium session on an iOS Simulator installs an app at session start with the `appium:app` capability, the app now installs without an app re-signing check. Simulator builds don't need re-signing. Previously, the session could fail before the app was installed, with an error stating that app signing is temporarily unavailable for the device.

Real iOS devices and Android devices keep the existing app re-signing behavior.
